subject: Capacity decision & rollout checkpoint for CardioSense Dedicated Pool
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference>
To: Thomas Li <thomas.li@cardiosense.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-07T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: dedicated capacity recap & immediate asks

Thomas — thanks for taking the call earlier. Quick recap from our side so we’re aligned and can move to proposal: 

What you stated as the main pain points:
- Frequent latency spikes during peak inference windows (even with smaller batch sizes) impacting SLA to clinicians.
- Need strong tenant isolation for PHI workflows (multi-tenant model serving today but want dedicated pool).
- On-prem-ish networking requirement: VPC peering + BYOK for KMS; audit logs & retention for 12 months.

Goals you asked us to hit:
- P95 latency target: <= 120ms for 512-token requests in steady-state.
- Baseline throughput: ~300 requests/min steady with burst to 1k reqs/min during overnight backfills.
- Go-live target window: early Jan (you mentioned Jan 8–15).

Preliminary sizing notes (attached sizing worksheet):
- Recommended reserved baseline: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (quantized 4-bit run for most models).
- Burst pool: 2 GPUs for short-term spikes (auto-burst to shared capacity if required).
- Canary plan: Gradual traffic ramp (10% → 50% → 100%) with automatic fallback to hosted model variant.

SLA & security: we can offer 99.9% uptime SLA for the dedicated pool + SOC2 evidence and audit logs. BYOK + VPC private control plane supported; we’ll include Ops acceptance checklist in the next doc.

Next steps we committed to on call:
1) I’ll share an initial commercial + technical sizing (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (security + infra) for the week of Nov 14.
3) Draft mutual action plan for signatures and timeline (first cut attached).

Can you confirm: the go-live target window above still works and the procurement contact is procurement@cardiosense.ai? If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update the sizing doc.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0193

-- attachments: call_recording_20261107.mp3; initial_sizing_estimate_cardiosense.xlsx; mudp_draft_cardiosense.pdf
From: Thomas Li <thomas.li@cardiosense.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference>
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@cardiosense.ai>, procurement@cardiosense.ai
Date: 2026-11-07T15:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: dedicated capacity recap & immediate asks

Ava — thanks, this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side:
- Security: VPC + BYOK are hard requirements. We also need HSM-backed KMS and key rotation policies documented.
- Data: PHI retention rules mean we’ll need audit logs and a 12-month retention SLA; please call that out explicitly in your Ops checklist.
- Timeline: procurement prefers a Jan 10 go-live target; that gives us time for an internal security review.

I’ve attached the usage forecast we ran this morning — it shows the overnight backfill pattern (spike through 02:00 local). If you can size the burst profile to handle that 90th-percentile spike we’ll be in good shape.

Thomas
Head of Infrastructure — CardioSense
thomas.li@cardiosense.ai | +1 (650) 555-4422

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-07T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up: dedicated capacity recap & immediate asks (internal)

Notes and proposed internal asks — quick and practical: 
1) Sizing confirmation: 8 reserved GPUs baseline + 2 GPU burst pool (hot standby autoscale). We should recommend quantized LLM runtimes and provide expected token cost range; ask Research for model quantization risks.
2) SLA: mark 99.9% uptime + p95 latency SLA for 512 tokens; legal will need to review downtime credits.
3) Canary & fallback: 3-step canary (10/40/100) with automatic fallback to a smaller hosted model (lower cost) in case of sustained latency/regression. Add traffic-shift runbook.
4) Security ops: Marissa, can you produce the Ops acceptance checklist (VPC peering steps, BYOK/HSM integration notes, audit log retention ops path) by EOD Nov 10? We’ll need that for the mutual action plan.
5) Commercial: propose a 12-month reserved commitment with monthly billing and an option to convert burst usage into short-term add-on spend. I’ll draft a range (ballpark) to share with Ava tomorrow.

Action owners: 
- Marissa: Ops checklist + SOC2 evidence summary (owner)
- Ava: Schedule technical deep dive and send MUDP link to CardioSense
- Ben: Draft ballpark commercial and fallback pricing tiers

Ben
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

Thomas / Alex —

Appreciate the quick confirmation. Per Ben’s internal notes above, next steps from Redwood: 
- We’ll run the technical deep-dive with our infra and security SMEs on Nov 14 at 10:00 AM PT (invitation incoming). Please confirm that time works.
- Marissa will share the Ops acceptance checklist by EOD Nov 10 (includes VPC peering steps, BYOK/HSM notes, audit log retention paths).
- Ben will circulate an initial commercial range and burst/pricing tiers by Nov 8.
- Draft MUDP (attached) — signing will lock in the Jan 10 go-live window and the 12-month commitment terms; procurement@cardiosense.ai, please confirm your preferred contract owner name and billing entity so we can populate the document.

If Nov 14 at 10:00 AM PT is tight, propose an alternate slot and we’ll flex. Once we have security sign-off in that deep-dive, we’ll push a formal SOW + Sizing + Ops runbook within 3 business days.

Thanks again — looking forward to locking this in.
